fhb-low-deposit.html: In September 2026, 50.3% of first-home mortgages approved across New Zealand (1,342 of 2,667 loans, or $850m in lending) were written with under a 20% deposit (>80% LVR), up from 46.0% a year earlier.
fhb-low-deposit.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table C31 (September 2026): 1,342 high-LVR (>80% LVR) FHB borrowers ($850m) out of 2,667 total FHB borrowers ($1,530m).
fhb-low-deposit.source_html:
HLF calculation: 1,342 ÷ 2,667 = 50.3% (Lending: $850m ÷ $1,530m = 55.6%)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Table C31 • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 10 November 2026.
fhb-low-deposit.name: First-home buyers using under 20% deposit (>80% LVR)
fhb-low-deposit.also_known_as: High-LVR (>80% LVR) first-home buyer share / Low-deposit FHB mortgage share
fhb-low-deposit.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Table C31
fhb-low-deposit.data_type: HLF-derived share & HLF-calculated comparison (from officially reported RBNZ loan counts & dollar values)
fhb-low-deposit.definition: The HLF-derived percentage of firm residential mortgage commitments to New Zealand first-home buyers where the Loan-to-Value Ratio (LVR) exceeds 80% (corresponding to under a 20% deposit), measured by borrower count alongside officially reported >80% LVR dollar lending.
fhb-low-deposit.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context (not measured in C31): RBNZ Table C31 reports all >80% LVR commitments as a single aggregate and does not disaggregate the underlying lending channel (such as bank low-equity speed-limit allocations, Kāinga Ora First Home Loans, or LVR-exempt new builds).
fhb-low-deposit.methodology: Compiled from monthly registered bank returns under RBNZ Table C31. First-home buyers are defined by lending banks as borrowers purchasing a residential property to occupy as a first home. Dollar values in Table C31 are published by RBNZ rounded to the nearest $1 million.
fhb-low-deposit.summary_text: In September 2026, 50.3% of first-home mortgages approved across New Zealand (1,342 of 2,667 loans, or $850m in lending) were written with under a 20% deposit (>80% LVR), up from 46.0% a year earlier.

fhb-share.html: In September 2026, New Zealand banks approved 2,667 first-home buyer mortgages totalling $1.53B—accounting for 20.3% of all new residential mortgage lending (up from 19.2% a year earlier), with an average loan size of $573,678.

HLF calculation: $1,530m ÷ $7,533m = 20.3% (Mean loan: $1,530m × $1m ÷ 2,667 = $573,678; RBNZ dollar series rounded to $1m)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Table C31 • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 10 November 2026.

fhb-loan-size-gap.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C31 by dividing total monthly dollar lending in each LVR tier (published by RBNZ in rounded $ millions) by the exact number of approved first-home borrowers in that same LVR tier.

borrower-income.html: In September 2026, approved New Zealand first-home buyer mortgage applications averaged $144,232 in gross borrower income (ranging from $123,000 to $197,000 across DTI bands).

borrower-income.source_html:
HLF calculation: FHB: $383.0m total band income ÷ 2,655.4 implied applications = $144,232 (subject to RBNZ band rounding)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Table C41 • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 10 November 2026.

borrower-income.data_type: HLF-calculated mean gross income across C41 TDTI bands (Total band income ÷ implied borrower count)
borrower-income.definition: The HLF-calculated mean annual pre-tax gross income across approved New Zealand first-home buyer mortgage applications (combining all single and joint applicants on the loan).
borrower-income.calculation: FHB: $383.0m total band income ÷ 2,655.4 implied applications = $144,232 (subject to RBNZ band rounding)
borrower-income.formula: Total Gross Income NZDm across all C41 TDTI bands ÷ Implied Application Count (Sum of [Band NZDm × 1,000 ÷ Band Avg Income NZD000s])
borrower-income.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: RBNZ Table C41 publishes band-level figures rather than a single nationwide mean; the overall figure is calculated by HLF from those published band figures. Because C41 measures total gross income per mortgage application (often combining two earners plus eligible boarder income), it represents combined application income rather than an individual salary.
borrower-income.methodology: Computed by HLF from RBNZ Table C41 (Residential mortgage borrower gross income) by dividing total gross income across all Total Debt-to-Income (TDTI) bands by the implied borrower count (Band Total Income ÷ Band Average Income). Note that RBNZ publishes band income pools rounded to $0.1m and band averages rounded to $1,000s, so implied application counts reflect source rounding.
borrower-income.summary_text: In September 2026, approved New Zealand first-home buyer mortgage applications averaged $144,232 in gross borrower income (ranging from $123,000 to $197,000 across DTI bands).

acc-weekly-compensation-claims.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: The 5.0% ratio compares annual weekly-compensation claim counts against total accepted injury claims (most of which are minor treatment-only visits). acc-weekly-compensation-claims.methodology: Sourced from ACC's Annual Report covering accepted injury claims, treatment/rehabilitation expenditure, and weekly compensation entitlements. Note: the two series measure separate annual claim counts (total accepted claims include non-earners and minor treatment-only injuries that do not require time off work).

kiwisaver-contributions-10yr.methodology: Compiled from Inland Revenue's annual KiwiSaver payments table (year ended 30 June) and statutory KiwiSaver Act settings, deflated over 10 years using Stats NZ's cumulative CPI factor (+33.7%).
kiwisaver-contributions-10yr.summary_text: Over the year ended 30 June 2026, total KiwiSaver contributions transferred to scheme providers reached $11.40B—up +123.5% from $5.10B in FY2016 (+67.2% after CPI inflation)—comprising $6.64B (58.2%) from employees, $3.72B (32.6%) from employers, and $1.04B (9.1%) in Crown contributions (with the statutory default rate at 3.5% EE / 3.5% ER from 1 April 2026 and the maximum annual Government contribution at $260.72).
